newsitem.title: UK: UK's CWS to begin criminal proceedings over bid.
newsitem.headline: UK's CWS to begin criminal proceedings over bid.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) said on Thursday it would commence criminal proceedings against suspended CWS manager Allan Green for theft and also against Andrew Regan and David Lyons "for aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring the theft and for handling stolen property".

In a statement, the mutually-owned group, which has been fighting takeover attempts by Regan's Galileo Group, said it would also begin civil proceedings against British merchant bank Hambros and law firm Travers Smith Braithwaite. Hambros acted as advisor to Galileo and Regan's Lanica Trust during the bid attempt, which earlier collapsed.
UK's CWS to begin criminal proceedings over bid=2
A CWS spokesman told Reuters the proceedings would begin with a private prosecution. "CWS has been the victim of a carefully conceived, planned and executed conspiracy," it said.

The latest move by the CWS results from earlier court action it took to secure the return of confidential information obtained by 31-year-old entrepreneur Regan and his advisors. On Wednesday, Lyons said the information had been "provided voluntarily by an employee of CWS".

Seven boxes of documents, including internal CWS minutes and board papers, were returned to the High Court on Wednesday and a hearing is scheduled for Friday to decide if the CWS injunction against the use of the information will be made permanent.
CWS said it had been advised there was "clear evidence that both these organisations (Hambros and Travers Smith Braithwaite) acted in breach of an equitable obligation of confidentiality to CWS".
It said they "had no credible grounds for believing that there was any legitimate basis for Regan to have any such documents" but "they proceeded to make unauthorised use of those...documents".

Earlier Galileo, an offshoot of Guernsey based investment trust Lanica with several important City backers, said it would not be pursuing its proposals to turn the 153-year-old supermarkets to funeral parlours group into a limited company which it would then offer to buy. The 1.2 billion pound $1.9 billion) bid had been widely expected to emerge last week but was thwarted by the CWS legal action. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
